Course Details

Subject {L-T-P / C} : BM4302 : Bioseparation Techniques { 3-0-0 / 3}

Subject Nature : Theory

Syllabus

Module 1 :

Module 1: Basic Concepts of Various Bioprocesses and Bioproducts
Sugars, Vitamins, Amino Acid, Proteins, Nucleic Acid, Polysaccharides, Various types of cells, Organic Acids etc.
Module 2: Removal of insoluble
Filtration: Filtration at constant pressure and constant rate, batch and continuous filtration, centrifugal and cross-flow filtration, Centrifugation: principles and design parameters, Microfiltration.
Module 3: Isolation of product
Cell Disruption, Various Techniques, Mechanical, Chemical and Biological Disruption Techniques, extraction, adsorption, ultrafiltration, precipitation
Module 4: Purification of Products
Adsorption, elution chromatography, ultrafiltration, electrophoresis, precipitation: Salting out and solvent precipitation, Chromatographic separation: size exclusion chromatography, ion exchange chromatography, affinity chromatography, Paper chromatography, thin layer chromatography, high-performance liquid chromatography (HPLC), Osmosis and reverse osmosis, Dialysis, Distillation, Crystallization.
Module 5: Polishing
Crystallization, drying, auxiliary process, solvent recovery, water preparation

Course Objective

1 .

To learn about various types of separation techniques for the isolation and purification of biologically important products.
2 .

To equip our UG students with key bioseparation technologies
3 .

To solve various problems
they may encounter in their further research and/or industrial practice

Course Outcome

1 .

1. Students will be able to learn about various types of separation techniques for the isolation and purification of biologically important products in industrial scale.
2. Students will be able to apply the principles of major bioseparation operations used in a bioprocess industry such as filtration, centrifugation, extraction and chromatography, precipitation, coagulation and flocculation.
3. Students will be able to design the bio-separation process units in the industrial level.
4. Students will be able to do engineering analysis and troubleshooting for bioseparation unit..
5. Students will be able to estimate scale-up calculations for bioseparation equipment.

Essential Reading

P. A. Belter, E. L. Cussler and W.S. Hu, Bioseparations: Downstream Processing for Biotechnology, Wiley-Interscience

2 .

J.E.Bailey and D.F.Olis, Biochemical Engineering Fundamentals, McGraw-Hill Education

Supplementary Reading

1 .

D. Forciniti, Industrial Bioseparations: Principles and Practice, Wiley-Blackwell

2 .

J.E.Bailey and D.F.Olis, Biochemical Engineering Fundamentals, McGraw-Hill Education

Course Details

Subject {L-T-P / C} : BM2764 : Biomaterials Laboratory { 0-0-3 / 2}

Subject Nature : Practical

Syllabus

Module 1 :

1. To determine the tensile and compressive strengths of implant materials.
2. To evaluate the coefficient of friction and wear resistance of different implant surfaces.
3. To measure the rheological properties of solvent/solution.
4. To study the influence of surface roughness on the wettability of implant materials.
5. To determine the contact angle on an implant surface using the sessile drop method.
6. To fabricate nanofiber scaffolds by the electrospinning process.
7. To conduct surface modification on medical implants using physical and chemical methods.
8. To fabricate 3D porous scaffold by freeze drying method
9. To conduct surface coating on metallic implants by electrochemical methods.
10. To determine the corrosion rate of metallic implants in simulated body fluid.
11. To evaluate the hemocompatibility of biomaterials.
12. To synthesize nanoparticles by the chemical route.
13. To investigate the drug release kinetics from biomaterial-based carriers.
14. To analyze the in vitro mineralization of bioactive materials.
15. To fabricate 3D bioprinted scaffold using 3D bioprinter.

Course Objective

1 .

To provide hands-on experience in evaluating the mechanical properties of biomaterials by determining tensile and compressive strengths, friction coefficient, and wear resistance of implant materials.
2 .

To develop an understanding of surface properties by studying wettability, roughness, and surface modifications using physical, chemical, and electrochemical techniques.
3 .

To enhance knowledge of biomaterial fabrication and characterization through experiments on nanofiber scaffold fabrication, nanoparticle synthesis, drug release kinetics, and in vitro mineralization.
4 .

To develop competency in assessing biomaterial biocompatibility and degradation through hemocompatibility and corrosion studies

Course Outcome

1 .

1. Students will be able to explain the concepts of stress and strain, and the parameters used to characterize the physical bulk and surface properties of materials.
2. Students will be able to describe the composition, structure and mechanical properties of the main classes of biomaterials- metals, ceramics, polymers, composites and the body tissues.
3. Students will be able to explain how composition, structure and treatment modify the mechanical properties.
4. Students will be able to describe the interactions of biomaterials with the biological environment - stability, corrosion, and hemo-compatability.
5. Students will be able to describe and give an example of how biomaterials are used to fabricate devices for clinical use.

Essential Reading

1 .

Wujing Xian, A Laboratory Course in Biomaterials, CRC Press

Supplementary Reading

1 .

NA, NA, NA

7076.b:
Course Details

Subject {L-T-P / C} : ME6142 : Fundamentals of Tribology { 3-0-0 / 3}

Subject Nature : Theory

Syllabus

Module 1 :

Module 1: Introduction (2 hours)
Introduction to tribology, history of tribology, inter-disciplinary approach, economic benefits.
Module 2: Surface contact (4 hours)
Introduction to surface, surface roughness and its measurement, conformal and non-conformal contact geometry, types, and stresses in non-conformal contact.
Module 3: Friction (6 hours)
Causes of friction, adhesion theory, abrasive theory, junction growth theory, laws of rolling friction, friction instability, friction of nonmetallic materials.
Module 4: Wear (6 hours)
Introduction, Wear mechanisms, adhesive wear, abrasive wear, corrosive wear, fretting wear, wear analysis, delamination theory of wear, wear debris analysis, wear testing methods.
Module 5: Bearings and Lubrication (10 hours)
Boundary lubrication, basic equations for fluid film lubrication, hydrodynamic journal bearing, liquid lubricants: properties and measurement, additives.
Module 6: Surface engineering (4 hours)
Introduction, surface treatments, surface coatings, methods, and procedure.
Module 7: Advanced topics on tribology (4 hours)
Biotribology, Tribology on mechanical components, Tribology of MEMS

Course Objective

1 .

Provide fundamental knowledge of tribology and its interdisciplinary significance.
2 .

Analyze surface contact, friction, and wear mechanisms in engineering applications.
3 .

Explore lubrication principles and their role in reducing friction and wear.
4 .

Introduce surface engineering techniques for enhancing material performance.
5 .

Introduction advanced topics of tribology such as biotribology

Course Outcome

1 .

CO1: Understand and apply tribological principles to analyze friction, wear, and lubrication in mechanical systems.
2 .

CO2: Evaluate surface contact characteristics and their influence on tribological performance.
3 .

CO3: Analyze and compare different wear mechanisms to predict material degradation and improve component lifespan.
4 .

CO4: Apply lubrication techniques to minimize friction and enhance system efficiency.
5 .

CO5: Utilize surface engineering methods to improve the durability and reliability of engineering components.

Essential Reading

1 .

Ian Hutchings, Philip Shipway, Tribology: Friction and Wear of Engineering Materials, Butterworth-Heinemann Ltd , 2020

2 .

Kenneth C. Ludema, Oyelayo O. Ajayi, Friction, Wear, Lubrication: A Textbook in Tribology, CRC Press , 2021

2 .

A. Cameron, C. M. Mc. Ettles, Basic Lubrication Theory, Ellis Horwood Ltd, Publisher , 2024

Journal and Conferences

2 .

Course Details

Subject {L-T-P / C} : PH5105 : Quantum Materials and Devices { 3-0-0 / 3}

Subject Nature : Theory

Syllabus

Module 1 :

(7 hrs) Introduction to Quantum Mechanics, Schrödinger equation, Wave packet, Normalization, Uncertainty principle, Infinite square well, Particle in a box, Free particle, Barrier potential, Quantum tunneling
Module 2 :

(7 hrs) Basics of Solid-State Physics, Crystal structure and Bravais lattices, Reciprocal lattice and Brillouin zones, Energy bands in solids: Free electron model and nearly free electron model, Bloch’s theorem and origin of bandgap, Concept of effective mass and holes
Module 3 :

(6 hrs) Concept of low-dimensional systems: Quantum wells (2D), wires (1D), and dots (0D), Density of states in 0D, 1D, and 2D systems, Quantum Confinement in Low Dimensions, Graphene and Carbon Nanostructures, Band structure and properties of graphene, Introduction to carbon nanotubes and their properties, Applications of graphene and carbon nanotubes
Module 4 :

(7 hrs) Basic Quantum Materials, 2D Materials Beyond Graphene and their bandgap properties, Introduction to magnetic quantum materials: Ferromagnetism, antiferromagnetism, and paramagnetism, Superconducting Materials, High-temperature superconductors and their applications, Fabrication and Characterization of Quantum Materials
Module 5 :

(9 hrs) Basic Quantum Devices, Quantum Dot based Single-Electron Devices, Single-electron transistors (SETs), High-electron-mobility transistors, Quantum Wells based Optoelectronic Devices, Graphene based transistors, Spintronic Devices, Giant magnetoresistance (GMR) and tunneling magnetoresistance (TMR) devices, Magnetic sensors and memory (MRAM)

Course Objective

1 .

To impart knowledge on
Introduction of the fundamental concepts of quantum mechanics and solid-state physics relevant to quantum materials.
2 .

Providing a basic understanding of key quantum materials, including low-dimensional systems like quantum wells, graphene, and nanostructures.
3 .

Explaining the working principles of elementary quantum devices and their practical applications.
4 .

Developing problem-solving skills and basic experimental knowledge required for studying quantum systems.
5 .

Encouraging students to think critically about how quantum materials and devices impact modern technologies.

Course Outcome

1 .

Upon successful completion of the course, students will be able to:
CO1: Explain key quantum phenomena in materials, such as quantum confinement, Dirac fermions, and topological states.
2 .

CO2: Analyze the properties of low-dimensional materials and predict their behavior in devices.
3 .

CO3: Demonstrate understanding of quantum device architectures, including quantum dots, single-electron transistors, and spintronic devices.
4 .

CO4: Demonstrate the ability to apply quantum principles to solve real-world problems in nanotechnology and materials science.
